review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

4:1.sourceText: Οἱ κύριοι, τὸ δίκαιον καὶ τὴν ἰσότητα τοῖς δούλοις παρέχεσθε, εἰδότες ὅτι καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔχετε Κύριον ἐν οὐρανῷ.
4:1.targetText: The masters: give that which is righteous and equal to the servants, having known that you also have a Master in the heavens.

groups.note: N1904 οὐρανῷ is singular in heaven; LSV heavens corresponds to the TR plural οὐρανοῖς. The heaven noun is linked without claiming identical number.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek repeated article nominalizes equality; English equal is coordinated with righteous without a second nominal marker.

4:2.sourceText: Τῇ προσευχῇ προσκαρτερεῖτε, γρηγοροῦντες ἐν αὐτῇ ἐν εὐχαριστίᾳ,
4:2.targetText: Continue in the prayer, watching in it in thanksgiving,

4:3.sourceText: προσευχόμενοι ἅμα καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν, ἵνα ὁ Θεὸς ἀνοίξῃ ἡμῖν θύραν τοῦ λόγου, λαλῆσαι τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ Χριστοῦ, δι’ ὃ καὶ δέδεμαι,
4:3.targetText: also praying for us at the same time, that God may open to us a door for the word, to speak the secret of the Christ, because of which I have also been bound,

groups.note: The genitive nominal constituent τοῦ λόγου specifies the purpose/content of the door and is rendered for the word; for is not taught as the standalone lexical meaning of the article.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

4:4.sourceText: ἵνα φανερώσω αὐτὸ ὡς δεῖ με λαλῆσαι.
4:4.targetText: that I may reveal it, as it is necessary for me to speak.

4:5.sourceText: Ἐν σοφίᾳ περιπατεῖτε πρὸς τοὺς ἔξω, τὸν καιρὸν ἐξαγοραζόμενοι.
4:5.targetText: Walk in wisdom toward those outside, redeeming the time,

4:6.sourceText: ὁ λόγος ὑμῶν πάντοτε ἐν χάριτι, ἅλατι ἠρτυμένος, εἰδέναι πῶς δεῖ ὑμᾶς ἑνὶ ἑκάστῳ ἀποκρίνεσθαι.
4:6.targetText: your word always being seasoned with salt in grace—to know how it is necessary for you to answer each one.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

4:7.sourceText: Τὰ κατ’ ἐμὲ πάντα γνωρίσει ὑμῖν Τυχικὸς ὁ ἀγαπητὸς ἀδελφὸς καὶ πιστὸς διάκονος καὶ σύνδουλος ἐν Κυρίῳ,
4:7.targetText: Tychicus will make known to you all the things concerning me—the beloved brother, and faithful servant, and fellow-servant in the LORD—

4:8.sourceText: ὃν ἔπεμψα πρὸς ὑμᾶς εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο, ἵνα γνῶτε τὰ περὶ ἡμῶν καὶ παρακαλέσῃ τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν,
4:8.targetText: whom I sent to you for this very thing, that he might know the things concerning you, and might comfort your hearts,

groups.note: Know is the shared lexical verb; N1904 γνῶτε is second-person plural, versus LSV/TR third-person he might know. The incompatible English subject he is not attached to this Greek verb.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness person difference: N1904 ἡμῶν means us/our affairs, while LSV concerning you follows TR ὑμῶν.
Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness subject difference: N1904 γνῶτε is second-person plural you may know; LSV he might know follows TR third-person γνῷ. No he subject is expressed or implied by this N1904 verb.
Source-witness object difference: LSV concerning you follows TR ὑμῶν; N1904 says concerning us, ἡμῶν.

4:9.sourceText: σὺν Ὀνησίμῳ τῷ πιστῷ καὶ ἀγαπητῷ ἀδελφῷ, ὅς ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν· πάντα ὑμῖν γνωρίσουσιν τὰ ὧδε.
4:9.targetText: with Onesimus the faithful and beloved brother, who is of you; they will make known to you all things that [are] here.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplied in the Greek attributive the-things-here phrase.

4:10.sourceText: Ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Ἀρίσταρχος ὁ συναιχμάλωτός μου, καὶ Μᾶρκος ὁ ἀνεψιὸς Βαρνάβα, (περὶ οὗ ἐλάβετε ἐντολάς, ἐὰν ἔλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς, δέξασθε αὐτόν,)
4:10.targetText: Aristarchus greets you, my fellow-captive, and Marcus, the nephew of Barnabas (concerning whom you received commands—if he may come to you, receive him),

groups.note: LSV renders ἀνεψιός as nephew; the Greek kinship word is normally cousin. This is a rendering/kinship distinction, not a different Greek reading or a claim that the usual relationship is identical.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

4:11.sourceText: καὶ Ἰησοῦς ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰοῦστος, οἱ ὄντες ἐκ περιτομῆς οὗτοι μόνοι συνεργοὶ εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, οἵτινες ἐγενήθησάν μοι παρηγορία.
4:11.targetText: and Jesus who is called Justus, who are of circumcision: these [are the] only fellow-workers for the Kingdom of God who become a comfort to me.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula/article supplied with the nominal these-only-fellow-workers statement.

4:12.sourceText: ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Ἐπαφρᾶς ὁ ἐξ ὑμῶν, δοῦλος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, πάντοτε ἀγωνιζόμενος ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐν ταῖς προσευχαῖς, ἵνα σταθῆτε τέλειοι καὶ πεπληροφορημένοι ἐν παντὶ θελήματι τοῦ Θεοῦ.
4:12.targetText: Epaphras greets you, who [is] of you, a servant of Christ, always striving for you in the prayers, that you may stand perfect and made full in all the will of God,

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness name omission: N1904 says Christ Jesus; LSV servant of Christ follows the shorter TR reading without Ἰησοῦ.

Source-witness verb difference: N1904 πεπληροφορημένοι is fully assured/fully convinced, from πληροφορέω; LSV made full follows TR πεπληρωμένοι, from πληρόω. The different original verbs are not silently treated as identical.
Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness verb difference: LSV made full follows TR πεπληρωμένοι (filled/completed), not N1904 πεπληροφορημένοι (fully assured).
Bracketed English copula supplied in the attributive of-you phrase.

4:13.sourceText: μαρτυρῶ γὰρ αὐτῷ ὅτι ἔχει πολὺν πόνον ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν ἐν Λαοδικίᾳ καὶ τῶν ἐν Ἱεραπόλει.
4:13.targetText: for I testify to him that he has much zeal for you, and those in Laodicea, and those in Hierapolis.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness noun difference: N1904 πόνον means toil/trouble, while LSV zeal follows TR ζῆλον.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness noun difference: LSV zeal corresponds to TR ζῆλον, not pinned N1904 πόνον (toil/trouble).

4:14.sourceText: ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Λουκᾶς ὁ ἰατρὸς ὁ ἀγαπητὸς καὶ Δημᾶς.
4:14.targetText: Lucas greets you, the beloved physician, and Demas;

unmappedSource.reason: Repeated Greek attributive article before beloved has no separate English word.

4:15.sourceText: Ἀσπάσασθε τοὺς ἐν Λαοδικίᾳ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ Νύμφαν καὶ τὴν κατ’ οἶκον αὐτῆς ἐκκλησίαν.
4:15.targetText: those in Laodicea greet you—brothers, and Nymphas, and the assembly in his house;

unmappedSource.reason: Rendering/argument-direction difference: N1904 Ἀσπάσασθε is second-person plural imperative Greet (the brothers…); LSV instead has those in Laodicea greet you, reversing giver/recipient roles.
Source-witness name/gender difference: accented N1904 Νύμφαν with later αὐτῆς (her) represents Nympha; LSV masculine Nymphas/his follows the alternative reading.
Source-witness pronoun gender difference: N1904 αὐτῆς means her, whereas LSV his follows TR αὐτοῦ.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness name/gender difference: LSV Nymphas with his follows the masculine reading; N1904 Νύμφαν with αὐτῆς (her) represents Nympha.
Source-witness pronoun gender difference: LSV his is masculine (TR αὐτοῦ); N1904 has feminine αὐτῆς, her.

Rendering/argument-direction difference: Greek commands readers Greet the brothers; LSV makes those people the subject of greet you and supplies an object you. This is not the same grammatical proposition.

4:16.sourceText: καὶ ὅταν ἀναγνωσθῇ παρ’ ὑμῖν ἡ ἐπιστολή, ποιήσατε ἵνα καὶ ἐν τῇ Λαοδικέων ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀναγνωσθῇ, καὶ τὴν ἐκ Λαοδικίας ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀναγνῶτε.
4:16.targetText: and when the letter may be read with you, cause that it may also be read in the assembly of the Laodiceans, and the [letter] from Laodicea that you also may read;

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English noun supplied in the second coordinated object; Greek has only the article τήν before from-Laodicea.

4:17.sourceText: καὶ εἴπατε Ἀρχίππῳ Βλέπε τὴν διακονίαν ἣν παρέλαβες ἐν Κυρίῳ, ἵνα αὐτὴν πληροῖς.
4:17.targetText: and say to Archippus, “See to the ministry that you received in the LORD, that you may fulfill it.”

4:18.sourceText: Ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τῇ ἐμῇ χειρὶ Παύλου. μνημονεύετέ μου τῶν δεσμῶν. ἡ χάρις μεθ’ ὑμῶν.
4:18.targetText: The salutation [is] by my hand, Paul. Remember my bonds. The grace [is] with you! Amen.

groups.note: Actual dative article and hand noun jointly supply by ... hand as the writing-instrument relation. The intervening my retains its separate actual possessive-adjective anchor; no independent Greek by preposition is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.
English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.
Source-witness ending difference: LSV includes Amen (as TR ἀμήν), absent from pinned N1904, which ends ὑμῶν.
